items.title: Fossil fuel emissions fall due to Iran war, renewables: research
items.description:
Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall slightly in 2026 due to the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock sparked by the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday.
Emissions from the burning of oil, gas and coal — the main drivers of climate change —rose by 0.9 per cent per year on average in the past decade, hitting a record high in 2025, according to the Global Carbon Budget report.
But they are expected to drop by 0.4pc in 2026, according to the research, published as nations meet at the UN’s COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye.

items.title: ESSAY: FOOD SECURITY AS SOVEREIGNTY
items.description:
AI-generated image
    
The claim that agriculture was never meant to be an income-generating activity sounds strange in an age that measures everything by return on investment. But no country can sustain its economy without securing its food supply. Food comes before the economy. It is the ground the economy stands on.
Farmers, of course, must earn a living. But that is only part of the question. The larger issue is how the state regards the sector. A government that treats agriculture purely as a business expects it to pay for itself, absorb its own risks and survive or fail on its margins.
